meta.name: spam_detection
meta.title: Spam detection
meta.description: Dev set for harness tuning: new items in the same style as the golden spam_detection set.

is_spam.instructions: Is `email` unwanted mail the recipient never asked for, such as bulk advertising, a scam or a phishing attempt?

is_phishing.instructions: Does `email` impersonate a trusted party to get the recipient to hand over passwords, payment details or personal data, or to open a malicious link or attachment?

tags.legit_personal: Legitimate personal email from friends or family.
tags.legit_work: Legitimate workplace email from colleagues, managers, clients or internal teams.
tags.legit_transactional: Legitimate receipts, confirmations, bills or shipping notices for something the recipient did.
tags.legit_security_alert: Genuine security notice from the real service domain, with no credential request.
tags.legit_newsletter: Marketing or newsletter mail the recipient clearly opted into (account reference, unsubscribe).
tags.spam_promo: Unsolicited bulk advertising for products or services.
tags.spam_seo: Unsolicited SEO, link-building, lead-list or agency marketing pitches.
tags.spam_crypto: Unsolicited crypto, investment or get-rich-quick schemes.
tags.spam_prize: Fake prizes, lotteries or 'you've been selected' offers.
tags.spam_scam: Advance-fee, romance or job scams that don't impersonate a party the recipient trusts.
tags.spam_obfuscated: Spam using obfuscated spelling (V1agra, spaced letters) to evade filters.
tags.spam_image: Image-only or 'see attached flyer' advertising with little text.
tags.phishing_credential: Impersonates a trusted service to harvest login or card credentials.
tags.phishing_invoice: Fake invoice, receipt, payment-change or malicious document attachment.
tags.phishing_bec: Business email compromise: impersonates a colleague or executive to get gift cards, wires or payroll changes.
tags.phishing_delivery: Fake courier or postal notice asking for a fee or personal details.
tags.phishing_tax: Fake tax-authority refund asking for bank, card or identity details.
tags.phishing_it: Fake IT helpdesk asking for passwords, MFA codes or re-registration.
tags.easy: A shallow keyword reader would get this right.
tags.hard: A careful reader gets it right, but surface cues (urgency, salesy tone, polish) point the wrong way.

input.email:
From: Dmitri Volkov <dmitri.volkov@inboxer.example>
To: Hannah Pike <hannah.pike@inboxer.example>
Subject: Tomatoes while I'm away

Hi Hannah,
Thanks again for offering to keep an eye on the garden while we're in Lisbon.
The hose is behind the shed and the side gate code is the same as last summer.
Please help yourself to any tomatoes that ripen, there will be far too many for us.
Back on the 19th. Dmitri

rationale: A neighbour follows up on a favour already agreed in person, with shared personal details and no offer or request for data.

input.email:
From: Ines Carvalho <ines.carvalho@mailspot.example>
To: Rafael Carvalho <rafael.carvalho@mailspot.example>
Subject: PAY ME BACK (lovingly)

Rafa!
I got the two tickets for the Morning Tides show on the 8th, row F like you wanted.
Your half is $58. Send it whenever, the usual way is fine, no hurry at all.
Also Mum says you still have her blue casserole dish. Return it before she notices!
Ines

rationale: Despite the shouty subject and a money request, this is a sister asking her brother to repay half of tickets he asked for, through their usual method, with no link or urgency.

input.email:
From: Tobias Lindt <tobias.lindt@ostranderfreight.com>

input.email:
From: Finance Operations <finance-ops@ostranderfreight.com>
To: All Staff <staff@ostranderfreight.com>
Subject: ACTION REQUIRED: September expenses due Monday

Hello everyone,
The September close starts Monday, so any expense claims not submitted by then will roll into October.
Please file them in Expensa as usual and attach itemised receipts for anything over $25.
We will never ask you to email card numbers or send receipts to an outside address.
Questions go to the #finance-help channel.
Finance Operations

rationale: An all-staff month-end reminder from the company's own finance domain uses an urgent subject but points to the usual internal tool and explicitly asks for no card details.

input.email:
From: Keystone Self Storage <office@keystonestorage.com>
To: Abigail Moss <abigail.moss@homemail.example>
Subject: Notice of rate change for unit B-214

Dear Abigail,

input.email:
From: Quayside <no-reply@quayside.app>
To: Femi Adeyemi <femi.adeyemi@fastmail.example>
Subject: Your Quayside password was changed

Hi Femi,
The password for your Quayside account was changed on October 9 at 21:14.
If this was you, there's nothing else to do.
If it wasn't, open the Quayside app and choose Account > Security to lock your account, or contact support from the Help menu.

input.email:
From: Orchard Mobile <security@orchardmobile.com>
To: Wen Zhao <wen.zhao@inboxer.example>
Subject: We blocked a SIM swap request on your line

Hi Wen,
Today at 10:42 someone in a store asked to move your number ending 4471 to a new SIM. Because they couldn't give your account PIN, we refused.
Your line is working normally. You don't need to reply to this message.
If you want extra protection, add a port-out lock under Settings in the Orchard Mobile app. Orchard Mobile staff don't request account PINs by email or text.

rationale: An alarming account-takeover alert comes from the carrier's real domain, says the attempt was blocked and asks for nothing, pointing only to the official app.

Hi Gabe,

Attention homeowners!

input.email:
From: Nathan Ellery <nathan@pixelharbor-studio.example>
To: owner@kilnworksstudio.com
Subject: Thoughts on kilnworksstudio.com

Hi there,
I spent a few minutes on kilnworksstudio.com this morning and really liked the class photos.
I did notice the site loads slowly on phones and the booking page isn't showing up in local search results.
We've helped over 40 studios like yours triple their bookings. Would you be open to a 15-minute call this week? I can send a free video audit first.
Best, Nathan Ellery, Growth Lead, Pixel Harbor Studio

rationale: A personalised-looking cold pitch from an agency the studio never contacted sells web and local-search services; it is unsolicited marketing but impersonates no one.

input.email:
From: Voicemail Service <voicemail@vm-notify-center.example>
To: yuki.abe@ostranderfreight.com
Subject: You have (1) new voice message - 0:47

input.email:
From: Renata Solis <renata.solis@ostrander-freight.com>
To: payroll@ostranderfreight.com
Subject: Year-end audit - need employee file today

Hi,
Our external auditors have asked for a copy of the full employee list for this year: names, home addresses, dates of birth and Social Security numbers.
Please export it as a spreadsheet and send it to me directly by end of day. I'm in sessions with them all afternoon, so email is best.

From: SwiftPost Customs <duties@swiftpost-customs-pay.example>

Your international parcel is being held at customs.
An import duty of $3.95 must be paid before it can be released.

From: State Department of Revenue <taxpayer-services@revenue-statecredit.example>
To: marisol.ortega@postbox.example
Subject: Your 2025 household energy credit has been approved

Dear Taxpayer,
You qualify for the 2025 household energy credit of $412.00 under the state rebate program.

From: Network Services <netops@tidewaterbooks-it.com>
To: gabe.lorimer@tidewaterbooks.com
Subject: VPN certificate renewal - complete before Monday

Hi Gabe,
Our VPN security certificates are being renewed this week. Staff who don't update will lose remote access on Monday morning.
Please run the attached updater and, when prompted, enter your network username and password to re-enroll your laptop.
This takes about two minutes. Thanks for helping us keep the network secure.
